question: Define the three methods for analysing limit states of shallow foundations in Eurocode 7 (direct, indirect, prescriptive) and explain how they differ.
gold_answer: Direct: separate ULS and SLS analyses; ULS models envisaged failure mechanism; SLS uses serviceability calculation | Indirect: comparable experience with field & lab results; choose SLS loads to satisfy all limit states | Prescriptive: conventional & conservative rules and control of construction; presumed bearing resistance
answer:
The three methods for analyzing limit states of shallow foundations in Eurocode 7 are:

- Direct: Carry out separate analyses for each limit state, both ultimate (ULS) and serviceability (SLS). (Section 3.2.1 [3.2.1])
- Indirect: Use comparable experience with results of field & laboratory measurements & observations. Choose SLS loads to satisfy requirements of all limit states. (Section 3.2.1 [3.2.1])
- Prescriptive: Use conventional & conservative design rules and specify control of construction. Use presumed bearing resistance. (Section 3.2.1 [3.2.1])

These methods differ in their approach to analyzing limit states:
- The Direct method involves separate analyses for ultimate and serviceability limit states.
- The Indirect method relies on experience and observations to determine serviceability loads that satisfy all limit states.
- The Prescriptive method uses established design rules and focuses on controlling construction.
